initial_failure.resolution: Old version rollback test expected an optional import failure to abort startup. Current Source explicitly warns and continues; actual diagnostic named bad release import. Update the direct consumer to assert inactive entry plus warning, close its running host, then qualify rollback. Production startup behavior is unchanged.

verification_scope_reason: Actual OS shared/exclusive locks are checked within one process and with real Python children. An admission gate prevents a new host or installer entering the lifetime-lock release/reacquire gap. One host promotes its own shared lease for mutation, refuses another existing host without terminating it, restores its original shared ownership on failed promotion or body exception, rejects nested/closed/foreign/boolean capabilities, and releases both locks on abrupt process exit. The native store borrows an explicitly validated exclusive lease without closing it; ordinary stopped installers remain refused while any host is running. Original install/upgrade/rollback, actual process-exit journal recovery, damaged-generation and lease consumers pass. Original Source optional/required startup diagnostic tests substantiate the corrected legacy consumer.
legal_adaptation: OS-owned admission/lifetime lock coordination is a Python runtime requirement beyond the Source package write lock. Supplied exclusive lease capabilities are profile-specific and serialized; no public boolean bypass exists. Promotion is allowed only for a single host and does not itself perform HMR or mutate packages. It must be composed inside an owned quiesced runtime operation.
activation_boundary: Lease and store ownership primitives only. Running manager/HMR integration, backend mutation command and production promotion remain pending.
